title: AI Travel Planner
tagline: A full-stack trip planner that turns destination, budget, days and interests into a day-by-day itinerary.
overview: A React front end walks the user from choosing a destination, through trip preferences — travellers, days, budget, travel style and interests — to a generated itinerary with day-by-day plans, places, stays and dining. Trips are saved through an Express REST API backed by MongoDB, which also models places and flight routes.
problem: Planning a trip means juggling budget, duration, group size and what everyone actually wants to do. Generic itineraries ignore those constraints; building one by hand takes hours.
motivation: A good exercise in full-stack design: a multi-step UI with real state, a REST API with related data models, and a clear seam where an AI model can generate the plan.
objectives: Collect trip constraints in a guided, low-friction flow
Produce a structured itinerary shaped by those constraints
Persist trips with references to places and flights
Keep the itinerary generator behind a single function so an AI model can replace it
features: Preference screen: travellers, days, budget, travel style and interests
Generated overview with daily budget, interests and a day-by-day itinerary
Places, accommodation and dining recommendation cards
Express REST API with CRUD for trips, places and air routes
Mongoose models with references (Trip → Places, Trip → AirRoute) and query filters

workflow.title: Pick a destination
workflow.detail: Search or choose a suggested city.

workflow.title: Set constraints
workflow.detail: Travellers, number of days, budget, travel style and interests.

workflow.title: Generate
workflow.detail: The plan builder produces an overview, daily budget and a themed day-by-day itinerary.

workflow.title: Explore
workflow.detail: Browse suggested places, stays and dining for the destination.

workflow.title: Save
workflow.detail: The trip is stored through the REST API in MongoDB.

decisions.title: Generator behind one seam
decisions.detail: Itinerary generation lives in a single function, so the current rule-based builder can be swapped for an LLM endpoint without touching the UI.

decisions.title: Relational shape in a document store
decisions.detail: Trips reference Place and AirRoute documents and are populated on read, keeping shared data in one place.

decisions.title: Filterable endpoints
decisions.detail: Places and routes support case-insensitive city, category, source and destination filters for search screens.

challenges.challenge: Keeping the app usable without an AI key
challenges.solution: The plan is generated locally from the user’s preferences, so the full flow works out of the box.

challenges.challenge: Keeping credentials out of the repository
challenges.solution: The MongoDB URI is read from a local .env file that is git-ignored.

testing: Runs locally with the Vite dev server and the Express API connected to MongoDB.
limitations: The current itinerary is template-based: preferences shape the day themes and budget, but the plan is not generated by an AI model yet.
Place, hotel and restaurant cards use generic names rather than live data for the destination.
No user accounts — saved trips are not tied to a person.
improvements: Replace buildPlan() with an LLM endpoint (e.g. Groq) that returns structured JSON
Real places and coordinates from a places/geocoding API such as Geoapify
Map view of each day’s route
verification: Written from the public AI-Travel-Planner repository (App.jsx, Server.js, route and model files, README).
